Sainik’s role
2022-02-17T00:00:00+06:00 | Mohammad Abdul Gafur
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/sainiks-role-2963761

In 1952, I was the editor of Sainik. I used to live in 19, Azimpur with Mr [Principal Abul] Kashem. I was present at the meeting of the All-party State Language Action Committee in Nawabpur [February 20, 1952]. The meeting decided not to violate section 144.

But in the face of students' demands it was concluded that violation of section 144 would depend on the role of students in the students' meeting at Amtala next day. If the decision of the working council is not accepted there, the council will be abolished naturally.

I was probably in Sainik's office at the time of the shooting. We published a special issue commemorating the language martyrs. Thousands of copies of the issue were sold in Dhaka within a very short time.

Around 3:00am, [February 23] police surrounded our magazine office. We were aware of such a move. Mr Kashem's wife, without opening the door, kept the police distracted by arguing with them about their activities and gave us enough time to escape safely.

We rushed through the graveyard and forest of Sheikh Saheb Bazar and tried to take shelter in some houses. But no one opened the door out of fear. As a result, Mr Kashem and I spent the night in a forest. Later in the early morning, we went to Nawabganj and found a shelter there. After spending some days in different shelters outside Dhaka, I came back to Dhaka.

Tamaddun Majlish had an extensive network outside Dhaka, and our local leaders actively participated in organising the Language Movement in different districts. Many of them were also arrested.

Mohammad Abdul Gafur was the editor of the Weekly Sainik during the Language Movement.

Source: Bhasha Andolon Shatchallish theke Baanna (Ed. Mostofa Kamal, Bangladesh Co-operative Book Society Ltd, 1987)

Translated by Shamsuddoza Sajen
